text:
viv: Opening a short PR that adds a canary rollout example for Dedicated capacity + a tiny Go SDK snippet showing isolation labels. Would love a quick sanity check before I link it in the handbook. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2501

noah: Nice. Can we include an explicit example of the canary weight & fallback policy? People often ask what happens when canary fails.

viv: Good point. Drafted this paragraph: \"Canary rollout: start 5% traffic to new tenant pool, monitor p99 latency and error-rate for 10 minutes, then increase by 20% increments. If p99 increases by >20% or errors >0.5%, automatically rollback to previous pool.\" Thoughts on numbers?

tara: Those thresholds seem reasonable as a default. Add a note that teams should tune thresholds per workload (LLM size, prompt length). Also include a tiny YAML example for the scale policy.

viv: Adding YAML: ```yaml
rollout:
  initial_percent: 5
  step_percent: 20
  evaluation_window_seconds: 600
  rollback_criteria:
    - metric: p99_latency_ms
      threshold_percent: 20
    - metric: error_rate
      threshold_percent: 0.5
```

gita: For the isolation example, please show how tenant_labels map to pool selectors and include a Go SDK snippet rather than only Python. A lot of platform teams use Go.

viv: Added Go snippet using the new client helper: ```go
client := redwood.NewClient()
req := redwood.CreateReservedPoolRequest{
  Name: "canary-eu-1",
  GPUs: 4,
  Labels: map[string]string{"pool": "canary-eu-1", "env": "canary"},
  ScalePolicy: &redwood.ScalePolicy{MinReplicas: 1, MaxReplicas: 8, CooldownSeconds: 120},
}
client.CreateReservedPool(ctx, &req)
```

noah: Love the Go example. Tiny nit: use `EvalWindowSeconds` in struct casing for Go example to match SDK convention. Also call out that `Labels` become selectors: `selector: pool=canary-eu-1,env=canary` in YAML.

viv: Fixed casing and added the selector example.

doc-bot: Linkcheck: no broken links detected. Suggested lint: add footnote explaining rollback satisfies immediate failover SLA for canary traffic.

sam: Small phrasing nit: avoid the term \"automatic rollback\" without describing who executes it. Suggest \"automated rollback triggered by the orchestration policy\".

viv: Updated wording to \"automated rollback triggered by the orchestration policy\". Also added a short troubleshooting checklist for canary flaps: 1) check selector label mismatch, 2) inspect GPU utilization and OOMs, 3) confirm network egress rules to model registry.

tara: Approving from docs perspective. :white_check_mark: Recommend we also add a short matrix mapping service-level-target (p50/p90/p99) expectations for canary vs steady state. Otherwise LGTM.

gita: approved from platform side. I can follow up with a link to the Go SDK usage page after merge.

doc-bot: CI: build OK, linkcheck OK, staged deploy passed.

viv: Merged. Release note: added canary rollout guide + Go SDK snippet; will follow up with a one-line crosslink to /sdk/go/client and a short note in Dedicated handbook about tuning thresholds per-model. Thanks all! :tada:
